name: OVR Technology
old_description: OVR has unlocked scent for video games with the Omara Scent Display.
about:
Based in Burlington, Vermont, OVR Technology develops hardware and software that add olfactory cues to interactive media. The company was founded by a team spanning industrial design, fragrance creation, neuroscience, and software engineering, though a founding year and ownership structure have not been publicly disclosed.

OVR’s core product line consists of the Omara Core and Omara Pro, personal scent displays that connect to PCs, mobile devices, and VR headsets via Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, or USB. The Core model offers ten scent channels and a desktop form factor, while the Pro provides sixteen channels in a pocket‑sized unit. Both devices mix up to three scent channels simultaneously and deliver bursts or continuous streams, with a time‑to‑perception ranging from 500 to 1,000 milliseconds.

The technology targets video‑game players and creators, with explicit support for PC and VR titles. OVR also partners with independent studios worldwide to integrate scent into their games, providing a software development kit and scent‑cartridge system that lets developers trigger aromas in sync with gameplay events.

The company positions itself as a first mover in digital scent, emphasizing the difficulty of pioneering the category. Its stated differentiation rests on the integration of hardware, proprietary Scentware® cartridges, and a software layer that synchronizes scent release with real‑time game data.

name: OXOS Medical, Inc
old_description: OXOS is transforming medical imaging with innovative, portable X‑ray solutions
about:
OXOS Medical, Inc. is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. The company was founded in June 2016 as Micro C, LLC, later renamed OXOS Medical, Inc., by Evan M. Ruff, who serves as CEO, and Gregory P. Kolovich, MD, a reconstructive hand surgeon who became frustrated with traditional imaging processes while at Harvard Medical School. That frustration inspired the development of the Micro C, the world's first portable Dynamic Digital Radiography device for orthopedic surgery.

OXOS designs and manufactures portable X-ray systems, including the original Micro C and the newer MC2, which received FDA 510(k) clearance (K252068) in 2024. The devices are built around a low-radiation profile while maintaining high image quality, and incorporate the AiLARA system, an automated technology that optimizes radiation dose according to the ALARA principle. A team of engineers, designers, and clinical advisors supports development and commercialization, with the MC2 now available in the United States.

The company targets orthopedics, pediatrics, and sports medicine, serving clinicians and medical practices nationwide. Testimonials cite use by hand and upper extremity surgeons, orthopaedic surgeons for professional sports teams (including the Jacksonville Jaguars), foot and ankle surgeons, and at off-road racing events through the non-profit Safety On Site. The portable systems are designed for point-of-care imaging in diverse clinical settings.

OXOS states its mission is to allow anyone, anywhere to access radiographic diagnostics at the point of need, expanding availability and changing how healthcare is delivered. The company emphasizes three pillars: safety through low radiation exposure, simplicity via portable and modular design, and intelligence through real-time diagnosis enabled by optimized alignment and a no-fire positioning system.

OceanHead Solar & Electric operates from Honolulu on the island of Oahu, Hawaii. The company is a licensed Hawaii solar and electrical contractor (LIC# C-33164) founded by Gail and Chelli, who are described as the owners and power couple behind the business. It is certified as a Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and a Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (DBE), and holds an A+ rating from the Better Business Bureau.

The firm designs and installs solar photovoltaic systems, battery backup, and electric vehicle charging infrastructure for residential and commercial clients. Its in-house licensed team manages projects from initial design through permitting and final installation, handling work that ranges from single-home rooftops to multi-building government contracts. The company also repairs orphaned systems left by other installers and performs electrical infrastructure upgrades, including multi-meter buildings and higher-voltage requirements.

OceanHead serves homeowners, commercial property owners, general contractors, manufacturers, and government agencies across Oahu. Commercial projects include flat-roof and carport-mounted solar arrays, fleet EV charging deployments, and full electrical system rebuilds. The company acts as a WOSB/DBE subcontractor on large-scale government solar and electrical work, and partners with contractors needing technical depth for complex installations.

The company emphasizes its local expertise with Hawaii's salt-air and high-UV conditions, designing each system around the specific roof type and structural capacity. It offers an Energy Service Agreement that covers the upfront cost of all services, and manages Hawaiian Electric net-energy-metering applications as part of every commercial installation. The founders state their mission is to make solar and battery storage attainable and long-lasting with no barriers to commitment.

Oceanside Welding & Fabrication operates from Oakland Park, Florida, serving Broward and Palm Beach counties. Menagh started the business on the principle of doing the job right with pride. The company emphasizes clean welds, corrosion-resistant materials, transparent quoting, and dependable timelines. Ohio Semitronics, Inc. is based in Hilliard, Ohio, and has been manufacturing electrical transducers and sensors since its founding in 1964. The company’s core business is custom electrical measurement devices, including a full line of standard transducers for AC/DC current, AC/DC voltage, watt-VAR, multifunction, frequency, power factor, signal conditioning, relays, switches, integrators, and panel meters. Ohio Semitronics combines deep engineering expertise with modern CAD and 3D printing technologies to move from concept to working prototype in as little as three weeks, while also supporting volume production of catalog devices.

Its customers span petroleum and petrochemical, electric utility, solar and wind energy, test and measurement, automation and control, and naval surface and subsurface applications. The firm has a track record with defense and industrial clients requiring high-accuracy sensors for critical environments.

Ohio Semitronics differentiates itself through a deep understanding of the inner workings of electrical measurements, enabling it to engineer sensors that achieve high accuracy, functionality, and durability in demanding application environments. The company emphasizes rapid prototyping throughput and an impeccable track record on challenging measurement projects.

Ohio Woodworking attributes its longevity to core values of quality, ingenuity, perseverance, humor, and family—principles the firm says are built into every project. Olson Solar Energy operates from Onalaska, Wisconsin, with additional bases in La Crosse, Eau Claire, and Wausau, serving customers across Wisconsin, eastern Minnesota, and northern Iowa. Customers are primarily homeowners and businesses seeking to reduce energy costs and carbon footprints. Installations have been completed in communities such as Onalaska, La Crosse, Mindoro, Viroqua, Green Bay, and Eau Claire. The company also works with referral partners and offers financing options to lower upfront barriers.

The founders emphasize a commitment to fast turnaround — aiming to complete every project in the shortest timeline possible — and a consultative approach that begins with a no‑cost evaluation using only an address and an energy bill. Orbis Electric is headquartered in Santa Rosa, California. The company was founded by Marcus Hays, a U.S. Navy veteran and EV pioneer who set land-speed records on electric motorcycles, along with co-founders Chance Claxton and Scott Streeter. Hays began the venture with a vision to revolutionize electric propulsion through advanced axial-flux permanent-magnet motor technology, drawing on experience from the CALSTART Advanced Transportation Hatchery in Burbank.

The company develops axial-flux in-wheel motors (its Ring Drive Wheel) and the COOL•E platform, an intelligent power-recovery system for AI data centers that combines EV-derived drive technology, orchestrated controls, and predictive diagnostics across CDUs, pumps, fans, and chillers. Manufacturing capabilities include additive manufacturing, CNC machining, and casting. Orbis holds 16 issued patents and 40 pending applications, and collaborates with Ames National Laboratory and Oak Ridge National Laboratory on next-generation magnetic materials such as Cerium Gap and MAGMA technologies.

Orbis serves electric mobility (including a four-year validation program with Volkswagen Group in Germany), electric transport refrigeration (eTRU), defense propulsion, and AI data-center infrastructure. Its cooling platforms target megawatt-scale liquid cooling for 800 V DC-native architectures supporting next-generation AI compute, with customers referencing NVIDIA chip roadmaps.

The company states it was started to engineer more performance from less — born in electric mobility, proven in demanding applications, and reimagined for AI infrastructure. It positions its automotive- and defense-grade motor technology as a way to reduce cooling overhead, reclaim white space, protect uptime, and lessen dependence on critical mineral supply chains.

about:
P.A. Electronics Corporation operates from Hartland, Wisconsin, where it was founded in 1995 as a veteran-owned and operated business. The company marks its 30th anniversary in 2025, reflecting three decades of continuous service in the magnetics sector.

The company designs and manufactures military and commercial transformers, inductors, and coils. Its capabilities span custom magnetic component design, quick-turnaround prototyping, and full-scale production of control transformers, audio transformers, toroidal transformers, current transformers, 50/60 Hz and 400 Hz transformers, three-phase units, Scott‑T and synchro/resolver transformers, and VERNISTAT models. In‑house environmental testing includes vibration and shock validation per military standards. The firm maintains a catalog of thousands of existing designs to meet immediate demand.

Primary customers include military procurement agencies and commercial OEMs requiring components qualified to MIL‑PRF‑27 (Grades 4 and 5), MIL‑T‑27, MIL‑T‑16315, MIL‑STD‑981, MIL‑I‑45208, MIL‑STD‑202, J‑W‑1177, MIL‑E917, and MIL‑STD‑2000. Parts are searchable by PA Electronics part number, national stock number (NSN), and military or commercial part numbers, supporting both defense and industrial supply chains.

The company emphasizes its veteran ownership, rapid prototype turnaround, extensive design library, and in‑house environmental test capability as key differentiators. Its founding purpose was to provide reliable, specification‑compliant magnetics with the agility to deliver custom solutions on short notice.

The shop provides precision molding, custom cable assemblies and connectors, printed circuit board assembly (including surface-mount, through-hole, BGA and micro-BGA), box builds, additive manufacturing, rapid prototyping, in-house tooling design and fabrication, and cleanroom sterile barrier packaging. P1 emphasizes its integrated in-house model—tooling, molding, electronics assembly and cleanroom packaging under one roof—to reduce lead times and supply-chain risk. The employee-owned structure is cited as a driver of accountability and precision.

about:
Pacific Die Cut Industries (PDCI) is headquartered in Lebanon, Kentucky. The company traces its origins to 1989 when it opened in the San Francisco Bay Area to address a shortage of custom automotive converting suppliers for Toyota and General Motors, offering just-in-time delivery and quality parts. No founders are named, and ownership structure is not disclosed.

PDCI converts non-rigid and thin rigid substrates into precision die-cut components through processes that include multi-station rotary die cutting, kiss cutting, lamination, slitting (up to 72 inches wide), CNC knife cutting, and clean-room manufacturing. The firm operates more than 4,000 square feet of Class 10,000 clean-room space with Class 1,000 capability, and provides value-added assembly, kitting, packaging, engineering support, and just-in-time logistics. Headcount and annual volume are not published.

The company serves four primary markets: automotive, where it acts as a Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier of NVH gaskets, seals, and decorative interior trim to global OEMs; medical, producing clean-room components for wound care, diagnostic consumables, and wearable sensors; energy, converting photovoltaic films, adhesives, and conductive foils for solar and wind manufacturers; and electronics, laminating pressure-sensitive adhesives onto technical films, gaskets, and dielectric materials.

PDCI states its mission is to be the industry leader in custom conversion across medical, automotive, electronic, and industrial markets by delivering the highest quality in the shortest lead times. Its quality system emphasizes risk analysis (PFMEA), error-proofing (poka-yoke), and continuous improvement, supported by IATF 16949 and ISO 13485 certifications.

about:
PFI, a member of the Grote Company Family of Brands, is headquartered in San Antonio, Texas, with manufacturing operations in Algona, Iowa. The business traces its roots back more than 60 years to the KOFAB and Meyer Industries lines, which were later unified under the PFI name. Today it operates as a family-owned enterprise led by CEO Bob Grote and COO Jack Grote, part of a multi-brand group that emphasizes shared engineering and support resources.

The company designs and builds sanitary, custom-configured conveying and handling equipment for food processors. Its product lineup includes belt conveyors, bucket and incline conveyors, dumpers, horizontal motion conveyors, and vibratory conveyors and feeders. In addition to equipment manufacturing, PFI provides in-house installation, technical service, replacement parts such as belts, buckets, pulleys, and stainless-steel hydraulic cylinders, and maintenance training. The firm serves customers from two locations, integrating systems with other OEMs to deliver complete line solutions.

PFI serves a broad range of food sectors, including bakery, candy and confectionery, cereal, dairy, frozen foods, fruits and vegetables, meat, poultry and seafood, nuts, pasta, pet food, ready-to-eat meals, and snack foods. Reference customers cited by the company include Hormel, a bakery processor, a snacks processor, and a large food processor, as well as Grillo's Pickles, which expanded production using integrated solutions from the Grote family of brands.

PFI says its differentiation rests on five pillars: dependable solutions built for long-term viability, integration-ready designs that fit existing lines, sanitary construction that meets or exceeds regulations, a collaborative approach with customer teams and other OEMs, and a customer commitment that spans pre-project planning through post-installation support. Leadership attributes the company's culture to its family-run heritage, noting that the partnership with the Grote group was driven by aligned values as much as by capability fit.

PGT Energy Solutions operates from Phoenix, Arizona, serving homeowners and businesses across the state with solar and battery storage installations. The company does not publish a founding year, though it advertises more than 25 years of industry experience. Ownership details and founder names are not disclosed publicly.

The firm installs residential and commercial photovoltaic systems and integrates battery storage, including Tesla Powerwall units, to enable grid-charged load shifting. Its core service is designing systems that charge during off-peak utility hours and discharge during peak periods, reducing demand charges from Arizona utilities such as APS and SRP. The company also provides zero-down financing options and warranty support for installed systems.

Primary customers are Arizona homeowners seeking lower electricity bills and backup power, as well as commercial clients aiming to cut demand charges. The company works directly with rate structures from Arizona Public Service (APS) and Salt River Project (SRP), tailoring battery configurations to each utility’s time-of-use and demand-based plans.

PGT Energy Solutions differentiates itself through NABCEP-certified installers, an Arizona-based team, BBB accreditation, and status as an Arizona Local Certified Energy Partner. It emphasizes the 30% federal investment tax credit and state rebates for standalone battery installations, positioning its offerings as a way to achieve energy independence without requiring rooftop solar.

PMC SMART Solutions traces its roots to 1929, when two families founded Plastic Moldings Company in Cincinnati, Ohio, during the Great Depression. The business relocated to Shelbyville, Indiana, and remains privately owned by the founding family. President and CEO Lisa Jennings leads the fourth generation of family ownership; the company earned WBE and WOSB certification in 2013.

The firm specializes in complex engineering and technical solutions for difficult-to-mold, high-temperature components. Its core capabilities include high-temperature and implantable biomaterials injection molding, hyper-precision molding and insert molding to micron tolerances, scientific injection molding, insert and over-molding, and complete secondary operations and assembly. PMC also provides design and engineering services, technology development, and quality systems management.

PMC serves the medical device and automotive industries. It is a strategic supplier to Medtronic and has worked with Bosch Automotive. The company’s components are used in life-saving medical technologies and high-performance automotive applications.

PMC differentiates itself through its SMART Solutions™ framework, emphasizing real insight, real attention, and real confidence. The company highlights a track record of 100% success in external quality audits with first-time certification, and a culture built on core values of commitment, integrity, accountability, innovation, stewardship, and partnership.

name: PMJ Technology
old_description: We are able to deliver quality samples with a quick turn-around time and at a competitive cost.
about:
PMJ Technology traces its roots to 1987 when Sam Kim, a former executive at Daewoo Electronics, founded Daesam to bring Korean contract manufacturing expertise to U.S. clients. His son Walter Kim joined in 2013 to prepare the business for a generational handover, and in 2017 the company was rebranded as PMJ Technology Inc.—named for the initials of Walter’s three children. The family-owned firm operates a factory in Siheung City, South Korea, and a warehouse in Arlington Heights, Illinois, just outside Chicago.

As an EMS provider, PMJ offers prototyping, PCB assembly (single-layer, multi-layer, flexible, LED, and RoHS/lead-free), injection molding and tooling (including design, tool fabrication, rapid prototyping, and high-capacity production of plastic, metal, and insert-molded parts), cable harness assembly (standard and custom with complex multi-connector and over-molding capabilities), and turnkey box-build integration from component sourcing through final testing. The company handles projects ranging from small batches to large production volumes across its two sites.

Its customer base spans agricultural, commercial, consumer, electronics, and industrial markets, with specific experience in agriculture, commercial and industrial equipment, and consumer electronics.

PMJ emphasizes a partnership model, aiming to deliver cost-effective, results-driven manufacturing solutions.

about:
POPULAS Furniture is based in Boise, Idaho, where it designs and manufactures adjustable ergonomic furniture. The company was founded to address growing demand for affordable, accessible workstations across military, education, healthcare, and residential settings. Its products are engineered and built in the northwestern United States, with customer service staff also located domestically.

The product line spans desks, tables, computer workstations, therapy tables, kitchen and bath components, and workbenches. Each piece offers multiple adjustment modes—hand crank, motorized, knob-adjusted, tilt, and sit-to-stand—across series such as Accella, Approach, Equity, Infinity, Progression, and Vox. Manufacturing emphasizes American craftsmanship, with compliance to ADA requirements and ANSI/HFES ergonomic guidelines.

POPULAS serves the U.S. military, schools and universities, healthcare and rehabilitation facilities, residential kitchen and bath markets (including accessible design for disabled users), industrial workplaces, and general commercial offices. The company holds a GSA contract for federal sales and distributes through a dealer network.

The company differentiates itself through domestic production, a lifetime warranty on most items, real-time phone support from U.S.-based staff, and eligibility for LEED certification points. Its design philosophy centers on ergonomic standards and ADA compliance as a foundation rather than an afterthought.

name: PPSI
old_description: Our AS9100D-certified facility, IPC-610 trained technicians, and four decades of manufacturing expertise mean your products are built to spec and shipped on time, so you can focus on what's next.
about:
PPSI has been assembling electronics in Houston, Texas, since 1986. The company remains privately held and headquartered in Houston, where it grew from a small PCB assembly shop into an AS9100D-certified manufacturing partner.

Today PPSI provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing services under one roof: surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly with placement down to 01005 packages, custom cable and harness assemblies built to IPC/WHMA-A-620 standards, comprehensive testing including AOI, X-ray, flying probe, functional test and device programming, full box-build and electromechanical integration with conformal coating for harsh environments, and turnkey supply-chain management. The facility supports programs from new-product introduction through recurring production volumes, staffed by IPC-610-trained technicians operating within an AS9100D quality system.

The company serves military and aerospace, space and satellite, industrial, and energy and oil-and-gas customers. Its assemblies fly on defense and aerospace platforms, operate in downhole and pipeline equipment, and control complex industrial systems. PPSI’s high-reliability documentation control and process rigor are tailored for flight hardware and ground-support electronics that must not fail.

PPSI emphasizes stability from four decades in business, direct communication with the people building the product, flexibility in a high-mix environment, and the convenience of a Houston-based, U.S. manufacturing location that supports site visits and audits. The founding principle — build it right, deliver on time — still guides every order.

PV Tech is a solar installation contractor based in Honolulu, Hawaii, serving the island of Oahu. The company draws on over 50 years of combined industry experience among its team, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm designs and installs residential and commercial photovoltaic systems, handling every step in-house with its own licensed electricians and PV installers rather than subcontractors. PV Tech works with homeowners and commercial property owners across Oahu, including Kapolei. Testimonials cite installations for private residences—such as an 18-panel system that offsets winter electricity use—and note the company’s willingness to right-size projects rather than upsell.

The company says its differentiator is a client experience that is ‘joyful, easy and rewarding,’ built on transparent communication, a step-by-step consultation process, and a policy of never using subcontractors so that quality control remains internal.

Paarlo Plastics Inc. operates from an 80,000-square-foot facility in North Canton, Ohio. Founded in 1981, the company has spent more than four decades as a dedicated blow molding contract manufacturer serving the toy, medical, automotive, and safety industries.

Its three-shift operation supports capabilities from product design and tooling construction through secondary machining — punching, drilling, sonic welding — to final assembly, packout, and on-time, in-full (OTIF) shipment. Paarlo serves Tier 1 and Tier 2 automotive suppliers requiring PPAP-compliant components, major toy brands needing durable, color-consistent parts, and medical and wellness manufacturers demanding clean, defect-free non-invasive products. The company also supports safety-industry applications.

Paarlo differentiates itself through a lean engineering approach that optimizes designs for cost and quality, quick turnaround quoting, and a commitment to transparency and collaboration. Its ISO 9001:2015 certification underpins a quality policy focused on increasing customer satisfaction and continually meeting requirements.

old_description: Founded in 1965, the company initially produced wall panels using Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) foam. Recreational products such as ice coolers, surfboards, and swim rings evolved over the years.
about:
Pacific Allied Products Ltd was founded in 1965 in Kapolei, Hawaii, initially producing wall panels and Hawaiian Ice Coolers from expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam. The company later added recreational foam products such as surfboards and swim rings before expanding into construction materials through a 1985 partnership with AFM, Inc.

Today the firm operates a vertically integrated plastics campus spanning over 90,000 square feet of manufacturing and warehouse space with approximately 50 employees. Its capabilities cover EPS foam molding, injection molding, blow molding, preform production, and a complete bottling line that rinses, fills, caps, labels, shrink‑wraps and palletizes finished beverages. The PET division alone is capable of producing more than 200 million bottles per year, and recent filler and blow‑molding upgrades have increased co‑packaging output by over 60 percent.

The company serves Hawaii’s construction and roofing sector with insulation boards, contoured tapered tile, laminated roofing systems and insect‑resistant insulation. It also supplies the beverage industry — including major local water brands — with PET containers for soda, juice, milk and water, and provides co‑packaging services for bottled water.

Pacific Allied Products states that it is the only facility on the island to manufacture preforms, blow containers and co‑pack bottled water all under one roof. Its integrated management system is certified to ISO 9001 and FSSC 22000, reflecting a stated commitment to food safety, quality and continuous improvement.

Its product line encompasses die-cut materials, adjustable swivel-top sockets, clamshell sockets, compact manual-loading sockets, double-latch sockets, flex-to-board socket assemblies, and board-to-board connectors. Paricon also offers thermal management options such as Peltier or liquid cooling for high-density BGA probing.

Paricon serves industries including test and measurement, microwave and RF, wafer testing, and custom connector applications. Its solutions target high-speed digital, waveguide, and RF applications where traditional interconnects face limitations.

The company emphasizes continuous investment in proprietary technologies and R&D to stay ahead of industry needs, with a mission to deliver innovative elastomeric interconnect solutions that enable customers to push the boundaries of electronics design and manufacturing.

about:
Parkman Woodworks was founded in 2015 on Parkman Avenue in Silverlake, Los Angeles, California, starting with a pickup truck and a thousand dollars. The founders built their first pieces from sustainable wood in a friend's driveway. Graham Taglang has served as the public face of the company since its inception.

The company produces custom handmade wood and steel furniture, including conference tables, dining tables, bed frames, desks, coffee tables, bookshelves, consoles, and benches. Operations are based in a historic brick-and-timber textile mill that celebrated its 100th anniversary in 2023, where a six-person team handles in-house design, woodworking, iron fabrication, powder coating, and wood charring. All pieces are made to order, from raw material selection through final delivery.

Parkman serves residential clients and commercial accounts across corporate offices, restaurants, and hospitality spaces. Their trade program works with interior designers and architects on projects ranging from home office furnishings to large-scale restaurant installations. Notable product categories include live-edge dining tables, custom conference tables for boardrooms, and banquette seating for kitchen and dining areas.

The company's stated mission is to turn wasted wood into practical art while advancing the values of handcraft. They emphasize hyperlocal sourcing, using solid lumber recovered from naturally fallen Southern California trees and structures. Accountability, awareness, and achievement are cited as core values, with every team member involved from inception to inspection of each piece.

about:
Parts Inc. has operated from Great Bend, Kansas, for more than 50 years. The business is locally owned and operated by Kevin and Kenton Lockwood, who oversee a parts and service operation that began as a supplier to the surrounding agricultural and industrial communities.

The company stocks and supplies components across automotive, agricultural, industrial, and oilfield sectors. Its shop specializes in custom hydraulic and air‑conditioning hose fabrication, assembly, and repair, supported by an inventory of thousands of adapters and fittings for foreign and domestic applications. Additional offerings include automotive paints, truck equipment and parts (air brakes, lighting, exhaust, DOT items), starters, alternators, generators, batteries, mufflers and exhaust systems up to six inches, and a range of car, truck, and jeep accessories. Parts Inc. also restores and maintains a fleet of historic military vehicles — half‑tracks, jeeps, amphibious tractors, and tanks — known as the Old Warhorses Collection, and operates as a licensed firearms dealer (FFL, NFA, SOT) with optics, suppressors, and military‑surplus items such as ammo cans, jacks, tools, and footwear.

Customers include jobbers, dealers, fleets, and individual owners across central Kansas. Agricultural operators around St. John, Pratt, and Great Bend rely on the shop for high‑cycle hose assemblies during harvest; oilfield trucks near Macksville and Stafford use water‑transfer and suction hoses; commercial truck fleets on the US‑281 and Highway 50 corridors source air‑brake and DOT‑required parts. The military‑vehicle collection serves re‑unions, parades, and veteran‑honoring events, while the firearms counter serves licensed buyers.

The company emphasizes local turnaround — same‑day hydraulic hose assembly is often possible when components are in stock — and a broad fitting inventory that covers JIC, NPT, ORFS, and other standards, allowing operators to avoid shipping delays from distant distributors.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication for industrial customers. The company highlights its multi‑generational family ownership and recent transition to woman‑owned leadership as key differentiators, emphasizing long‑term local service and custom fabrication expertise.

about:
Patriot Equipment, headquartered in Minden, Nebraska, traces its roots to 1984 when Harold Lempka opened Minden Machine Shop in a 30-by-50-foot building along the railroad tracks. Initially a side venture with a partner, the shop repaired and built machinery using an old lathe and welder. After the partner departed, Harold's sons Larry and Kerry joined the business, and the operation transitioned from contract machining to manufacturing its own line of farm equipment.

Today the company operates across more than 92,000 square feet of production space with a workforce exceeding 60 people. It manufactures and sells 31 distinct equipment lines—seed tenders alone offer ten size and style variations—while maintaining a job-shop division that handles custom fabrication and repair work in steel, stainless steel, and aluminum. Capabilities include laser cutting, robotic and hand welding, bending, sawing, painting, assembly, and hydraulic and electrical integration.

The primary customer base is agricultural producers, but the shop also serves commercial firms, schools, and hospitals that require custom metalwork or equipment repairs. Products are sold directly and through a dealer network across the United States.

The business was built on a simple principle articulated by Harold Lempka: do a good job at a fair price and treat the customer with respect. That philosophy, combined with a deep sense of patriotism that inspired the Patriot Equipment brand in 1994, continues to guide the company's growth.

The company describes itself as a multi-national organization with global offices in the United States, Hungary, and Switzerland, though its founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed on its website.

The company also supplies Tone Commander secure SIP phones with JITC/STIG certifications and NSA-listed data diode kits for critical infrastructure protection.

Patton differentiates itself through U.S.-manufactured network equipment, a full-spectrum embedded solutions capability from feasibility to acceptance, and an ODMD model that allows customers to brand Patton-designed hardware. about:
Patton's Medical is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. The company traces its roots to Pattons Inc., which began selling custom medical air packages to hospitals in 1980. In 2008, the leadership created Patton's Medical to sell and service their own medical gas equipment nationwide. Since 2012, the business has been owned and operated by ELGi USA, which acquired Pattons Inc. and Patton's Medical as an entry into the U.S. medical equipment market.

The company designs, assembles, and services medical air systems built around Hitachi oil-less reciprocating scroll compressors (available in base-mount, modular, and tank-mounted configurations) and medical vacuum systems that use Busch oil-less, contactless multi-claw technology. It also supplies pipeline products — including fully automatic universal medical manifolds, outlets, zone valves, alarms, and architectural products — through strategic partnerships. Control panels are built to UL 508A standards, and all equipment is designed to meet or exceed NFPA 99 requirements. The firm offers custom package engineering for unique facility specifications and provides installation and ongoing service across the country.

Patton's Medical serves hospitals, clinical laboratories, and university research facilities that require compliant medical gas and laboratory air systems. Its products support applications such as surgical air, WAGD (waste anesthetic gas disposal), and general laboratory air supply. The company works directly with facility engineers, contractors, and medical gas consultants to specify and deliver code-compliant systems.

The business was started to move beyond distribution and offer proprietary, nationally supported medical gas equipment. Leadership emphasizes an "old fashion" commitment to customer service, backed by a team with deep backgrounds in sales, marketing, manufacturing, and engineering. When standard products do not fit, the company evaluates the application and develops special packages tailored to the facility's needs.

Renwick founded the venture on a lifelong passion for the decorative arts and a commitment to personal expression rather than trend-chasing. The differentiator lies in the fusion of historical reference with contemporary sensibility, executed through a transparent, human-scale supply chain that prioritizes material integrity and artisanal patience.

Penn Metal Fabricators Inc. was founded in 1969 in Ebensburg, Pennsylvania. The company operates a 175,000-square-foot facility there, housing complete fabrication and machine shops under one roof.

The shop performs all operations from raw material to finished part, working from customer drawings or CAD files. Capabilities include CNC laser cutting of sheet and tube, plasma cutting, punching, bending, automatic sawing, and tube bending; CNC vertical machining, horizontal milling and boring, and lathe turning; robotic and manual MIG/TIG welding; and finishing via powder coat, wet enamel, CARC, and chemical conversion coating. Customers span the U.S. Military, which has sourced troop-support equipment and spare parts for more than 40 years; the U.S. Postal Service, which buys bulk-mail handling equipment and sorting-room furniture; the construction sector, receiving scissor- and boom-lift components; and the railroad industry, where parts are welded into rail cars. The about-us page adds aviation, biomedical, and electrical markets to the list.

Penn Metal emphasizes its ability to deliver both one-off prototypes and long production runs on schedule, backed by an ISO 9001:2000 quality system and FaroArm CMM inspection. The firm says its combined staff experience exceeds 160 years and that its processes meet the strict requirements of both the military and the postal service.

Performance Systems Integration (PSI Conversions) operates from Brick Township, New Jersey, at 2029 Route 88. PSI manufactures LS and LT swap standalone wiring harnesses for GM Gen II, III, IV, and V engines, along with engine controller kits, transmission parts, and related conversion components. Harnesses are built using high‑temperature cross‑linked polyethylene TXL or GXL wire, with splices made on an ultrasonic wire welder and protected by high‑temp heat shrink. Terminals and connectors meet or exceed OEM specifications from Delphi/Aptiv, Yazaki, and Kostal. Every harness undergoes 100% functional testing on computer‑based Dynalab or Cirris equipment. The company also assembles engine controller kits and provides PCM programming services.

The primary customers are automotive aftermarket builders, hot‑rod shops, and individual enthusiasts performing LS/LT engine swaps. PSI’s product catalog covers a wide range of donor vehicles, including Chevrolet, Buick, Oldsmobile, Pontiac, Ford/Mustang, Nissan, Jeep, and Toyota platforms, as well as universal hot‑rod applications. A dealer program supports retail and installation shops.

PSI emphasizes domestic production, stating that its harnesses are made in the USA with top‑quality materials. It highlights a combined 25+ years of experience, phone support five days a week with 24/7 email access, and a commitment to shipping in‑stock harnesses within 1‑3 business days. The company’s original harness design is credited with setting the standard for the LS swap industry.

Perry's Metal Fabrication operates from Mooresville, North Carolina, in the heart of the Lake Norman region. The shop was founded by Tim Perry, who brings over 30 years of hands-on welding and fabrication experience to the business. It remains a family-owned operation, with Perry serving as both owner and lead fabricator. The company began as a skilled trade outfit focused on precision metalwork for local clients.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication, welding (MIG, TIG, stick, and soldering), bending, shearing, rolling, and CNC machining on lathes and mills. It works with aluminum, steel, stainless steel, 4130 chromoly, titanium, and sheet metal. Capabilities range from one-off brackets and frames to larger-scale production runs, including architectural metalwork such as gates, railings, and furniture frames, as well as repair and reinforcement of existing parts. The facility houses lathes, mills, and press brakes for cutting, shaping, and forming.

Customers include homeowners, small businesses, auto and marine enthusiasts, and industrial clients across the Mooresville and Lake Norman area. Concrete projects include a custom roll cage for an exotic auto shop, sprint car chassis modifications, a fabricated race hauler, a funnel and parts for a local ice cream shop, and a fabrication project for a national warehouse chain. The shop also serves motorsports teams with specialized race car fabrication.

The company emphasizes trust, communication, and treating every job as its own. Quick turnaround times are cited as a differentiator, and the shop coordinates with a third-party powder coating service to deliver finished parts. The focus on craftsmanship and customer satisfaction is presented as the core reason for the business's longevity.

name: Petoskey Plastics Inc
old_description: To earn the appreciation and respect of our customers, associates, and communities.
about:
Petoskey Plastics Inc. is headquartered in McKinney, Texas, but traces its roots to Petoskey, Michigan, where Duke and Paul Keiswetter founded the company in 1969. Operations began on April 1, 1970, with five employees and a single bag machine converting purchased film into plastic bags. The privately held, family-owned business added extrusion capability in 1975 and has since grown into a veteran-owned enterprise recognized as the 2023 and 2025 Veteran Business of the Year by the National Veteran Business Development Council.

The company operates four domestic manufacturing facilities — in Petoskey, Michigan; Morristown, Tennessee; Hartford City, Indiana; and McKinney, Texas — employing approximately 500 associates. Its vertically integrated process spans polyethylene film extrusion (with 98% of equipment capable of 3- and 5-layer technology), custom bag converting, shrink film production, and a 330,000-square-foot recycling facility in Hartford City that feeds recycled resin back into extrusion lines. A 4-color offset paper printing press at the Morristown plant supports private-label packaging.

Petoskey serves automotive, construction, home improvement, medical, institutional, retail, and private-brand markets, along with niche sectors such as janitorial, parks and recreation, and fundraising. Customers include OEMs and brand owners seeking custom-engineered flexible packaging, shrink films, and medical gowns, with the company highlighting its ability to incorporate up to 70% third-party certified post-consumer recycled content.

Founded on a sustainable mindset that began with in-house recycling in 1978, Petoskey differentiates itself through closed-loop recycling, vertically integrated manufacturing, and a culture described as “hands-on” from the production floor to the CEO. The firm emphasizes on-time, in-full delivery backed by in-house quality labs at each site.

about:
Phoenix Solar Panel Systems operates from Phoenix, Arizona, serving the metropolitan area and surrounding communities. The company was founded by Steven Smith, J.D., known as "Solar Steve Esquire," after he worked at several Valley solar companies and observed what he describes as an extreme lack of professionalism, honesty, and customer service in the industry. Smith started the business to provide a transparent alternative in a market he characterizes as having zero regulation and high turnover.

The firm does not perform installations itself. Instead, it helps homeowners and businesses explore solar options — grid-tied, off-grid, and battery-backup systems — and connects them with independent installers. Customers contract directly with the installer performing the work. The company also coordinates related services such as home energy audits, attic insulation, duct sealing, EV charger installation, solar water heaters, solar panel cleaning, bird proofing, removal and reinstallation, and solar carport or patio cover projects. It provides educational resources including an Arizona Solar FAQ, cost guides, and a list of questions to ask solar companies.

The primary customers are residential property owners in the Phoenix area and commercial property owners seeking to reduce energy costs. The company references work with Arizona Public Service (APS) and Salt River Project (SRP) utility territories. Commercial clients include businesses looking to cut operating expenses and meet clean-energy goals. The service also supports off-grid properties requiring custom battery and backup designs.

Smith states the company was created to bring honesty, integrity, and transparency to the solar industry. The model emphasizes educating customers rather than selling, presenting both positives and negatives of solar ownership, and building long-term relationships over short-term commissions. The founder describes the business as being in the "people business, not the solar business," with a goal of cleaning up the residential solar market through fair, informed decision-making.

Photonworks Engineering is based in Honolulu, Hawaii, and was founded in 2003 by Tim Johnsson. Johnsson, a recipient of the ABC 2010 Excellence in Construction Award for multi-family developments, established the company to connect people with cheaper and cleaner sources of power while preserving Hawaii’s natural beauty.

The company provides end-to-end energy solutions: solar photovoltaic design and installation, battery energy storage systems, microgrid engineering, full-service electrical construction, energy efficiency retrofits, PV system monitoring and maintenance, and eco-friendly development. Photonworks handles site assessment, engineering, permitting, construction, commissioning, and long-term operations and maintenance, offering up to two years of no-charge O&M after installation. It also structures power purchase agreements with zero capital expense and zero-down financing. The firm reports serving thousands of customers across Hawaii and beyond, with a project portfolio that includes commercial, institutional, and government sites.

Photonworks serves residential homeowners, commercial property owners, educational institutions, non-profits, and government agencies. Named projects include Hanalani Schools, Boys and Girls Club of Hawaii, Joint Base Pearl Harbor, Aiea Public Library, Kailua Waste Water Facility, Kahauiki Village, Hawaii Pacific University, Century West, USSF Space Fence, and the Board of Water Supply. The company works closely with Hawaiian Electric (HECO) on interconnection agreements and grid services.

The mission is to exceed expectations through one-stop engineering-to-construction solutions, straightforward technical staff rather than salespeople, and a focus on energy autonomy and resilience for Hawaii’s transition to 100% renewable energy.

Founded in 1992 in White Hall, West Virginia, Pick-Up City operates as an auto and truck recycling business under President Grant Kelly. The company serves Marion County and surrounding areas from a 78,000-square-foot indoor warehouse that stores more than 65,000 cataloged parts.

The operation disassembles late-model vehicles piece by piece, then cleans, inspects, and tests each component before entering it into a computerized inventory system. Parts range from engines, transmissions, and axles to doors, bumpers, windshields, and lighting assemblies. All inventory is housed indoors to protect against weather, and fluids such as freon, coolant, oil, gasoline, and brake fluid are recovered and recycled in accordance with environmental standards.

Pick-Up City supplies repair shops, collision centers, fleet operators, and individual vehicle owners throughout the region and nationwide via common carrier. Free regional delivery is offered, and customers can search the inventory online or visit the warehouse for in-person assistance.

The company emphasizes its indoor, climate-controlled storage, environmentally responsible fluid handling, and a searchable digital catalog as key differentiators. Select parts carry 30- to 90-day warranties, and the sales team provides personalized support for part identification and compatibility.

name: Piedmont Plastics
about:
The Londonderry, New Hampshire branch of Piedmont Plastics traces its roots to Plastic Supply, Inc., a local plastics distributor that served the region for more than 47 years. On September 12, 2019, Piedmont Plastics acquired PSI and integrated the operation into its North American network of branch locations. The facility is managed by Jaime Lemos.

The branch operates as both a stocking distributor and a fabrication shop. It carries a broad line of plastic sheet, rod, and tube — including acrylic, polycarbonate, nylon, acetal homopolymer and copolymer, fluorocarbon, UHMW, polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC, polystyrene, high-pressure laminates, and polyurethane. In-house fabrication capabilities span CNC routing and laser cutting, milling, drilling, turning, welding, bonding, edging, buffing, sanding, sandblasting, and thermoforming. The shop runs four Mori Seiki CNC vertical milling centers, a Mori Seiki AL2 CNC lathe, a Saeilo Sprint 20 CNC lathe, a Hardinge DSM59 lathe, four Bridgeport CNC vertical mills, a HAAS TM2P vertical milling center, a Drypoll vacuum thermoforming machine, a Gruenberg anneal oven, and an Accu Finish diamond grinder. Assembly services include mechanical fastening, welding, custom wiring harness assembly, bonding, riveting, and packing.

The location serves customers throughout southern and central New Hampshire, with listed service areas covering Manchester, Derry, Nashua, Salem, Merrimack, Hudson, and dozens of surrounding communities. While the company does not specify target industries in its public materials, the material range and fabrication services suggest it supports manufacturers, prototypers, and maintenance operations requiring plastic components.

The acquisition was intended to preserve PSI’s longstanding local presence while expanding Piedmont’s distribution footprint; no additional differentiators or founding mission are stated.

Pittsburgh Plastics Manufacturing was founded in 1977 by Jim Zona in Butler, Pennsylvania, just north of Pittsburgh. A Penn State graduate, Zona began by developing gel insoles—essentially "waterbeds for your feet"—and built the company into a women-owned custom manufacturer of gel and foam cushioning solutions.

Operating from a 91,000-square-foot facility with 50–75 employees, the company formulates more than 35 proprietary polymer blends—including IsoGel®, IsoFoam®, and GELoam®—and handles mold design, CNC machining, prototyping, and full-scale production in-house. An internal polymer scientist and CAD designer support rapid turnaround, while lean practices such as KAIZEN and 5S drive efficiency.

PPM serves medical and healthcare, safety, industrial, hot-and-cold therapy, and foot-care markets, supplying OEMs and private-label brands across the United States, Europe, and Canada. The facility is FDA registered, ISO 13485:2016 certified, and QRS-compliant with process validations for medical components, adhering to CGMP and TQMS standards.

The company emphasizes its U.S.-based, women-owned status and a "PPM Promise" of 100 percent precision, accuracy, and on-time delivery. Complete manufacturing traceability, pre-certified raw materials, and quality checks at every stage reinforce its differentiation in custom cushioning.

about:
Plantible Foods operates from Eldorado, Texas, where it produces Rubi Protein™, a proprietary ingredient derived from the aquatic plant Lemna.

The company grows Lemna on aqua farms that require no arable land and use a fraction of the water needed for conventional protein crops. The harvested biomass is processed to extract RuBisCO, marketed as Rubi Protein™, a complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids plus vitamin B12. The ingredient is neutral in flavor and free of major allergens.

Plantible sells its protein to food manufacturers formulating baked goods, plant-based meats, dairy alternatives, and sports nutrition products. In baked goods, the protein replicates the mouthfeel of butter and eggs or the elasticity of gluten; in plant-based meats it can replace methylcellulose binders while improving juiciness; in dairy alternatives it enhances texture and nutrition.

The founders frame the business as a response to a broken food system, aiming to deliver sustainable nutrition at scale. They cite the crop’s efficiency — ten times more protein per acre than soy with ten times less water — and its carbon capture as core advantages that differentiate the ingredient from other plant proteins.

about:
Popknot Wood operates from Rogers, Arkansas. The company was founded by John, a U.S. Army veteran, after he began teaching woodworking to his grandchildren in his home shop. What started as a family project building birdhouses, signs, and boxes evolved into a formal business when the family developed a marketing plan and launched a website. The venture is veteran-owned and family-driven.

The shop produces custom woodworking and restoration pieces using a mix of hand tools, power tools, CNC routing, and laser engraving. Its output includes furniture refurbishment, replacement parts for discontinued items, heirloom repairs, custom cutting boards (including state-shaped designs), wooden urns and memorial pieces, awards and presentation pieces, river tables, custom flags, and signs. All items are made in-house and shipped to all 50 states.

Customers range from individuals seeking personalized gifts or restored heirlooms to churches, ministries, and organizations needing faith-based creations, awards, or signage. The company serves residential clients, religious institutions, and corporate buyers looking for presentation pieces or custom signage.

John credits his Army service for instilling discipline and integrity that guide every build. Faith informs the work as a form of stewardship, and the shop prioritizes local wood whenever possible. Popknot Wood was recognized as the Best Woodworker in Rogers, AR for 2026, reflecting its commitment to purpose-driven craftsmanship.

about:
Porter Barn Wood operates from Phoenix, Arizona, where Thomas Porter founded the business in 2010 after years of woodworking experience. The company began when Porter and his friend Craig Suiter recognized a demand for quality reclaimed barn wood in the Phoenix area, initially unloading beams from Pennsylvania barns and opening a regular yard for public sales. Porter formed the LLC in 2012, and the venture has since grown into a family-owned operation with his wife Emy and their two children involved.

The company maintains a wood shop, metal shop, concrete shop, and finishing and contracting teams, allowing it to fabricate custom furniture, architectural accents, and structural elements from a wide range of materials. Services include milling, blacksmithing, CNC plasma cutting, CNC routing, laser engraving, and various finishing techniques such as lacquer, conversion varnish, and custom color matching. The shop also sources and sells reclaimed barn wood from Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, and Iowa, as well as live-edge slabs salvaged from local forest-fire and beetle-kill sites.

Porter Barn Wood serves restaurants, hospitality venues, commercial contractors, luxury home builders, and residential remodelers. Projects have included dining tables for Surf City and Famé, a creative event space for The Duce, and whole-home remodels featuring custom cabinetry and built-ins. The facility has also hosted film crews for HGTV and PBS productions, taking advantage of its well-lit, climate-controlled workshops.

The company distinguishes itself by accepting customers' own reclaimed materials — such as family barn wood or old warehouse metal — and integrating them into new builds. It also offers free woodworking and metalworking classes, rents its event tables, and emphasizes a collaborative approach with designers and architects to execute custom visions.

The store also supplies specialty threads (Aurifil, Isacord, Mettler, Superior), trims, ribbons, buttons, and notions. Two annual clearance sales — the Anniversary Sale in July and the Year End Clearance in December — attract regional buyers.

The company emphasizes professional advice and individualized service, a commitment it has maintained for 46 years. Its combination of a broad fabric inventory, machine sales and service, and an active education program distinguishes it from typical fabric retailers in New England.

Past projects include telematics, marine, space exploration, and U.S. military applications.

PowerFilm emphasizes application-specific design tailored to program constraints rather than standard product formats, controlled manufacturing with repeatable quality, and direct engineering collaboration with OEM, fleet, and government teams from early design through sustained production. about:
Pravi Apparel operates a U.S. sales office in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, while its manufacturing facility, known as Praville, is located in Haiti. Production began in January 2021 after founder Jim Weber built a solar‑powered plant in a town without running water or electricity. The venture started with a mission to create jobs and pull people out of poverty in Haiti, employing individuals like Elyse Ledix, who joined the team after being widowed.

The company produces only polo shirts, offered in four lines—Biz‑Wear, Pravi‑Golf, Wear‑Strong, and Dura‑Text. All shirts are assembled in Haiti using 100 % American‑made fabrics and feature a self‑fabric collar typically found in higher‑priced apparel. The solar‑powered factory has a capacity of up to 275 workers.

Pravi targets buyers of industrial‑strength uniform polos, golf polos, and workwear. Its shirts are marketed to businesses seeking durable, comfortable uniforms and to consumers looking for performance golf or casual wear.

Pravi’s differentiator is its social mission: for every 4,000 shirts sold, the company says it pulls one Haitian out of poverty. It keeps prices low by avoiding rent, property taxes, utilities, and tariffs, and by using interest‑free loans with no repayment timeline.

Its Prime Cutting Room provides custom cutting, packaging, and weighing of meats to customer specifications. Prime Source Foods serves over 3,000 customers through a network of sales representatives living throughout the service area, and offers an e-commerce app for mobile and desktop ordering.

Customers are primarily foodservice operators across New England and eastern New York, including restaurants, institutional kitchens, and hospitality venues. The distributor emphasizes all-natural and local product options alongside national brands.

Prime Source Foods states its mission is to meet customer needs with cost-competitive products and flexible, efficient distribution. Its vision targets becoming New England's most valued provider of center-of-the-plate products through superior sourcing, product knowledge, and service options. Core values cited are trust, fairness, respect, honesty, and teamwork.

name: Primitive Precision Metalcraft

about:
Primitive Precision Metalcraft operates from Minneapolis, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2007 by Hans Early-Nelson, whose path to metalwork began with a boat-building upbringing, a blacksmithing and furniture-making apprenticeship in Germany, a welding and machining diploma from Dunwoody Institute of Technology, and an internship with a local jeweler. In 2020, Liz Parent, a University of Minnesota art and design graduate with a decade of handmade jewelry experience, joined as chief operating officer. The couple, who also raise two children, run the business as a family-owned shop.

The shop focuses on architectural metal fabrication, producing landscape and garden structures, pergolas, countertops, shelving, hardware, functional housewares, feature stairs, handrails, wall coverings, edge details, and kick rails. A team of fabricators handles custom projects that range from residential handrails and vent hoods to larger structural installations. Facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Primitive Precision serves homeowners, designers, architects, and builders in the Twin Cities area. Past work includes custom-forged wedding rings, handrails, vent hoods, and architectural installations for both residential and commercial clients.

The company says it sets itself apart by matching old-world quality with modern innovative design, drawing on Hans’s mastery of joinery, blacksmithing, jewelry, and machining to create detailed, high-quality metalwork.

old_description: We invest in our people, equipment and technology to bring you the best packaging solutions available through quality, timeliness, relationships and sustainability.
about:
Priority Plastics Inc. is headquartered in Grand Prairie, Texas, and operates extrusion blow‑molding facilities across the United States. The company does not disclose its founding year or ownership structure, and no founders are named in public materials.

The company manufactures plastic packaging solutions including HDPE and PET containers, tight‑head pails, canisters, and dry‑pack towel wipes. Core processes are extrusion blow molding and injection stretch blow molding (ISBM), the latter marketed as a way to expand PET applications. A multi‑plant footprint enables coast‑to‑coast production, multi‑plant sourcing, and in‑plant customer‑service support. The firm also develops custom tooling and maintains an expanding library of stock tools to shorten lead times.

Priority Plastics serves customers ranging from startups to multinational firms in food and beverage, nutrition and wellness, industrial, personal care, agriculture, animal health, cannabis/hemp/CBD, hardware, hazardous materials, healthcare/nutraceuticals, and specialty chemicals.

The company emphasizes four pillars—quality, timeliness, relationships, and sustainability. Its GreenLite platform incorporates post‑consumer recycled (PCR) content and lightweight designs; the PriorityPour ECO line uses up to 80 % recycled core material. Public targets include sourcing 60 % of materials from recycled or renewable sources by 2035, making 80 % of products recyclable by 2028, and cutting Scope 2 and 3 emissions 30 % by 2030. All facilities recycle unused resin, and the geographically distributed network is positioned to lower freight costs and carbon emissions.

Private Label Specialties is based in Goffstown, New Hampshire, and was founded in 1991 by Ray Duhaime, who serves as president. The company began with a simple idea: offering custom-labeled sparkling water as an alternative to national brands like Poland Spring and Perrier, giving businesses a way to put their own name on a beverage.

In 1997 it added promotional products distribution, and in 2006–2007 brought screen printing, embroidery, and direct-to-garment printing in-house by acquiring its former vendor. The operation now runs a full-service apparel decoration shop alongside beverage production, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

The customer base spans restaurants, pizzerias, sub shops, catering companies, country stores, farm stands, and broader hospitality and service-based industries. Clients use the branded beverages for resale or as promotional giveaways, while the apparel and promo items (drawn from a catalog of over 750,000 products) support broader marketing programs.

The company says its “Unique Branding Advantage” rests on a trifecta of excellent price, impeccable quality, and outstanding service. Investments in technology allow it to move from concept to finished label in under an hour, and the founder’s original goal—helping businesses market themselves rather than big brands—remains the stated mission.

Pro-Forming Sheet Metal LLC operates from Norwich, Connecticut, where it has provided custom metal fabrication and machining services for more than 25 years. The company emphasizes a one-stop-shop approach, combining CAD design, CNC punching, forming, welding, machining, and finishing under one roof to control lead times and costs. It highlights its experienced craftsmen, with an average of over 20 years of industry experience, and its ability to hold tolerances to the thousandth of an inch.

ProCare Medical Equipment was founded in 2007 and is headquartered in Meridian, Idaho. The company began as a medical equipment provider focused on serving patient care facilities in the region.

ProCare specializes in the rental, sale, and servicing of durable medical equipment (DME) for healthcare facilities. Its services include equipment rental programs, repair and preventative maintenance on most brands, cleaning and sanitization under its proprietary Patient Ready Certified™ program, liquid oxygen delivery with respiratory therapy support, and continuing education for healthcare professionals. The company also assembles custom equipment packages tailored to skilled nursing, hospice, rehabilitation, and VA facilities.

ProCare serves long-term care facilities, rehabilitation and transitional care centers, hospice agencies, and VA or government healthcare facilities across Idaho and eastern Oregon. Its customer base includes skilled nursing facilities seeking wound care and bariatric equipment, hospice providers needing comfort-focused surfaces and bed frames, and government facilities requiring respiratory and rehabilitation solutions.

The company emphasizes compassionate, on-time service and a holistic approach called 360° Servicing, which integrates rental, repair, cleaning, and education into a single solution. Its Patient Ready Certified™ seal guarantees equipment sanitized beyond industry standards, and its Sunrise Sessions provide continuing education for clinical staff. ProCare states its mission is to empower health with innovative solutions and to become the primary DME provider for professional care agencies in its service area.

Process Equipment, based in New Waterford, Ohio, operates as an independent dealer of material handlers, attachments, and recycling equipment. The goal is to deliver a purchasing experience close to buying new without the new-machine price, backed by independent, expert advice.

It serves any industrial operation that relies on presses, machine tools, or automated production lines.

Justman emphasizes a vast vendor network that enables efficient and economical project execution, along with rapid response times and flexible scheduling. The business model was built on decades of hands-on repair experience and long-standing customer and vendor relationships.

Nasoya traces its roots to 1978, when its founders began producing tofu in a converted barn in Leominster, Massachusetts. In 2004 the brand was acquired by Pulmuone Foods, a South Korean food conglomerate, and today operates from a headquarters in Ayer, Massachusetts.

The company manufactures a range of tofu products — silken, firm, extra-firm, and super-firm — along with Asian-inspired items such as noodles, dumplings, and wonton wraps, and a line of ready-to-eat plant-based meals under the Plantspired brand. A 1987 facility expansion pushed output to more than 60,000 pounds of tofu per week, and a new Ayer plant slated for 2025 is described as the world’s largest tofu production line. Nasoya reports annual sustainability metrics that include recycling 80 tons of cardboard, treating 34.6 million gallons of wastewater, and reusing 3.4 million pounds of soy byproduct.

Nasoya’s products are sold in more than 25,000 retail grocery locations nationwide, serving the plant-based protein, organic food, and Asian-inspired food categories. The brand also partners with culinary institutions such as the Culinary Institute of America to support student scholarships and innovation challenges.

The company emphasizes organic, non-GMO soybeans sourced from local farmers, tray-free packaging, and closed-loop water and waste systems as key differentiators. Its stated mission is to make wholesome, plant-based eating accessible for every lifestyle through sustainable practices and flavor innovation.

Rework services address PCB component replacement, mechanical modifications, and packaging changes, with fulfillment for expedited shipping. The shop focuses on high-mix, low-to-medium volume production, from prototype through production runs.

Distributors such as TTI and Heilind Electronics, along with OEMs including LightSpeed Technologies, Forest Dental, Engle Dental Systems, and Warn Industries, have cited the company's responsiveness, quality, and supply-chain reliability.

name: Quantum Semiconductor LLC
old_description: Introducing a semiconductor technology platform that significantly expands the function and capability of silicon - revolutionizing what silicon can do with light.
about:
Quantum Semiconductor LLC is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company develops a semiconductor technology platform based on atomic-layer engineered Group-IV superlattices that extend silicon's ability to sense and emit light beyond the visible spectrum.

Its core technology combines Group-IV superlattices (carbon, silicon, germanium, tin, lead) with novel device architectures to produce high-gain, low-noise photodiodes, CMOS image sensors, LiDAR photodetectors, and optical receivers monolithically integrated with CMOS. The platform also enables superlattice heterojunction bipolar transistors for 5G and 6G wireless, as well as quantum sensing, computing, and random-number generation devices. The company holds 27 U.S. patents and 25 foreign patents, with 14 peer-reviewed publications.

The technology targets markets that rely on light sensing and imaging across ultraviolet, visible, and infrared wavelengths. Applications include CMOS image sensors for consumer and automotive cameras, silicon photonics receivers for data centers, LiDAR for autonomous vehicles and eye-safe ranging, high-frequency BiCMOS for next-generation wireless infrastructure, and quantum devices for secure communications. Quantum Semiconductor participates in the Southwest Advanced Prototyping (SWAP) Hub under the Department of Defense's Microelectronics Commons, indicating defense and aerospace engagement.

The company states its differentiation lies in overcoming silicon's fundamental optical limitations without requiring heterogeneous integration, delivering noiseless gain in photodiodes and enabling new functionality at minimal added manufacturing cost.

about:
QuantumScape was founded in 2010 and is headquartered in San Jose, California. The company develops solid-state lithium-metal battery technology aimed at transforming energy storage for a lower-carbon future.

QuantumScape designs and manufactures solid-state battery cells using an anode-less architecture that eliminates the graphite anode, relying instead on a nonflammable ceramic separator. Its Eagle Line pilot production facility in San Jose produces cells for automotive, data-center, aerospace, defense, and consumer-electronics applications. The product lineup includes the QSEV series for electric vehicles, the QSDC and QS PowerBlock systems for AI data centers, and the QSAS platform for aerospace and defense.

The company serves electric-vehicle makers, AI data-center operators, aerospace and defense contractors, and consumer-electronics brands. Its technology targets the need for higher energy density, faster charging, and improved safety in each of those markets.

QuantumScape says its anode-free design reduces material costs and simplifies manufacturing, while the ceramic separator removes the fire risk associated with liquid electrolytes. Removing graphite also addresses supply-chain concerns tied to a single geographic source.

about:
RAM Electronics Industries Inc operates from a 20,000-square-foot facility in Cinnaminson, New Jersey. The company has over 35 years of industry experience as a contract manufacturer, though a specific founding year and founder names are not disclosed. Ownership details are not publicly stated.

The firm specializes in electronic wire harnesses, cable assemblies, and electro-mechanical sub-assemblies for OEM customers. Its capabilities span automated cut/strip/terminate, crimping, soldering, IDC/ribbon cable termination, overmolding, labeling, and testing. The shop runs Komax and Schleuniger wire processing machines, TE/AMP terminators, and 3D printing for tooling, processing millions of feet of wire annually from prototype through large-scale production.

RAM serves medical equipment, telecommunications, amusement, audio/video, electronic data processing, gaming, and renewable energy sectors. Customers range from prototype runs to medium and high-volume orders, with the company emphasizing no job too large or small.

The company highlights its ISO 9001:2015 certification, ITAR registration, and IPC WHMA-620 compliance as quality differentiators. In-house engineering supports design-to-production transitions, and a broad inventory of connector tooling from brands such as TE, Molex, JST, and Hirose enables fast, cost-effective turnaround.

about:
RBB operates from Wooster, Ohio, where it has been manufacturing electronic assemblies since 1973. The company began as a specialist in printed circuit board assembly and custom industrial control panels, serving manufacturers who needed reliable, high-mix production.

Today RBB provides turnkey and labor-only PCB assembly, control panel assembly, wire and cable assembly, and new product introduction support. Its services span engineering review, component procurement, assembly, testing, and product lifecycle extension for legacy designs. The shop emphasizes recurring high-mix orders and maintains a customized process for each program.

Customers come from aerospace and defense, medical device and imaging, safety systems, power generation and backup for data centers, nuclear, alternative energy, automotive, instrumentation, process manufacturing control, and heavy equipment. The company cites its ability to handle complex, regulated builds across these sectors as a core strength.

RBB says it was founded to eliminate the headaches that manufacturers face with complex PCBA and control panel projects. It differentiates itself through over 50 years of process knowledge, a dedicated team that delivers recurring jobs on time, and certifications that meet aerospace, defense, and high-reliability requirements.

name: RBW
old_description: LED lighting design/manufacturing; 100,000 sq ft HQ/plant opened 2022
about:
RBW, an independent design and manufacturing company, was founded in 2007 as RBW Studio LLC and is headquartered in Kingston, New York. The company operates as a certified B Corporation, reflecting a commitment to social and environmental accountability alongside its lighting business.

RBW designs and manufactures LED luminaires — including sconces, pendants, flush mounts, and canopy fixtures — from a 100,000-square-foot facility that opened in Kingston in 2022. The plant houses design, engineering, and production under one roof, and the company offers a factory powder-coating service with color selection and shipping starting at 15 business days. Product data such as DWG, Revit, SketchUp, and photometric files are provided for each fixture.

The brand serves architects, interior designers, and national account clients across commercial office, hospitality, restaurant, residential, and workplace projects. Notable installations include the Noma restaurant in Copenhagen and offices of Fortune 500 companies throughout the United States. A dedicated national accounts program supports designers scaling atmosphere across multiple locations.

RBW’s “Different By Design” philosophy emphasizes that a product’s strength lies in how it is made, how it ships, and how it lasts. The company highlights quick, reliable delivery and keeps product specialists on call to assist with finish options and dimming science. Its founding goal was to change the game of lighting design while making a positive impact on the planet and community.
